question: Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2, & x < 0 \\ 3, & x \geq 0 \end{cases}$. Is $f(x)$ continuous at $x=0$?
explanation:
Left-hand limit: $\lim_{x \to 0^-} f(x) = 2$.

Right-hand limit: $\lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x) = 3$.

Since LHL $\neq$ RHL, $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x=0$.

options.B: No, $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x=0$ because LHL $=2$ and RHL $=3$
options.C: Yes, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$ because both one-sided limits are equal
options.D: No, $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x=0$ because $f(0)$ is undefined
